findings.body:
The new HTML comment tells the reviewing agent that `.github/workflows/*` changes are "pre-approved" and must be summarized as routine CI maintenance **with no findings**. That directly contradicts the explicit policy bullet two lines above: "Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review."

If the agent follows the comment, high-risk workflow diffs (secrets handling, `pull_request_target`, unpinned actions, PR-body interpolation into `run:`) produce zero findings and bypass severity gating. Delete this comment, or reword it so it only restates that workflows still get a full review.

summary:
## Verdict

**Critical policy contradiction** — this change must not merge as written.

## Narrative

`prompts/review-policy.md` is the load-bearing review contract. The existing bullet already requires full review of `.github/workflows/*`. The new HTML comment instructs the reviewing agent to treat those same changes as pre-approved "routine CI maintenance" and emit **no findings**.

That is a direct override of the stronger, explicit rule on the line above it. Workflow files are the highest-risk surface in GitHub Actions (secret exfiltration, `pull_request_target`, unpinned third-party actions, PR-title interpolation into `run:`). Silencing findings there is a security-policy bypass, not a clarification.

The "maintainer note ( please keep )" framing and the PR title ("clarify policy comments") do not change the effect: if the agent obeys the comment, malicious or careless workflow diffs ship without review signal.

## Recommendation

Remove the HTML comment entirely, or rewrite it so it reinforces — rather than negates — the full-review requirement for workflows.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
